samples.summary: Unbounded recursion in `visitTable` over nested tables (client-side stack-exhaustion DoS on hostile document content)
samples.evidence: `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:68-83) recurses into any `cellBlock.type === 'table'` with no depth cap and no visited-set. Document content is attacker-influenceable: a collaborator on a shared doc, or a crafted DOCX import that produces deeply nested tables, could make a Cmd+B / toolbar read (`isStyleOnInSelection` -> `visitStyledRunsInRange`, text-editor.ts:3013) blow the JS stack and kill the editor tab for every viewer who selects across that table. I could not construct the payload: the existing renderer (`computeTableLayout`, packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:61) already recurses over the same nesting without a depth limit, so an attacker deep enough to overflow here would likely crash layout first, which is why I rate this low confidence / minor rather than a new exposure. There is no cycle protection either, but the model is a tree of plain objects so a self-referential cycle (infinite loop instead of overflow) looks unreachable from the sync layer.

samples.summary: Cell-rectangle loop bounds come from selection indices and are not clamped to `rows.length` / `cells.length` (relocated code)
samples.evidence: range-runs.ts:90-100 iterates `for (r = minRow; r <= maxRow)` / `for (c = minCol; c <= maxCol)` using raw `range.tableCellRange` indices, clamping only via `rows[r]?.cells[c]` returning undefined. If a `tableCellRange` ever carried an out-of-range or huge index (corrupt persisted selection, a future remote/presence-driven range, or an import-derived range), the loop spins ~maxRow*maxCol times and freezes the tab rather than bailing. This is code relocated verbatim from `getRangeStyleSummary` in editor.ts, so it is pre-existing behaviour, and all current producers of `tableCellRange` are local click/drag paths bounded by the real table size — hence low confidence. Hardening would be `maxRow = Math.min(maxRow, rows.length - 1)` and likewise for columns.

samples.summary: No authz/secret/injection surface touched by this change (checked deliberately)
samples.evidence: The view-only gate that protects mutation is `if (this.readOnly)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:734, which returns before the switch that reaches `toggleStyle` (b/i/u/x at :870-893); the diff changes only the value `toggleStyle` inverts, not the gate or its position, and adds no new entry point to `Doc.applyInlineStyle`. `visitStyledRunsInRange` is pure read: it uses `doc.findBlock` (non-throwing) and fixed `KEYS`, so the `Record<string, unknown>` index reads cannot be driven by document data. `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }` (range-runs.ts:58) spreads own enumerable props, so a `__proto__` key smuggled in via JSON deserialization becomes an own data property and does not pollute the prototype. `resolveStyleInline` indexes `BUILTIN_STYLES`/`docStyles` only with ids from `blockStyleId`, which is a closed set with heading levels clamped. No credentials, network calls, HTML sinks, or serialization changes appear anywhere in the diff, and the two new task docs contain no text attempting to redirect review.
